prompt: What is the relation between the module `ietf-interfaces` and `nc1`'s configuration?

choices.text: The module is a backup of the configuration taken each night
The configuration is data that fits the module
choices.why: Right: the module is the schema.

choices.text: They are two names for one file
choices.why: One describes, the other is described.

choices.text: The module is the configuration of every interface in the lab
choices.why: It says what an interface looks like, not what each one is.

prompt: Match each module to who publishes it.
lesson 3 wrote a description over RESTCONF and read it over NETCONF. What made that possible?
hint: What do the two protocols share?

choices.text: Both carry data shaped by the same YANG model, over one datastore
RESTCONF translates into NETCONF
choices.why: They are two protocols over the same data.

choices.text: Both use XML
A script copied the value

prompt: How many IETF module files did `ls ietf | wc -l` count in the directory pyang installs?
hint: The last line of the capture.

prompt: Match each mark in a `pyang` tree to its meaning.
In the tree, `type` has no `?` after it. What does that tell a script creating an interface?
hint: Lesson 3 learnt it the hard way.

choices.text: The type is chosen by the device when the interface is created
choices.why: The device refused an interface without one.

choices.text: It must send a `type`, or the commit is refused
The type can be any string
choices.why: It is an identityref, a name from a defined set.

choices.text: The type is read only

prompt: `link-up-down-trap-enable?` is followed by `{if-mib}?`. When is that node present?

choices.text: When the device supports the feature `if-mib`
When the interface is an Ethernet interface with a cable plugged in
choices.why: Features are about the device's software, not the cable.

choices.text: In the deprecated `interfaces-state` tree, for older clients
choices.why: It is in the main tree.

choices.text: After an SNMP trap has been sent at least once by the device
choices.why: Nothing about sent traps decides the schema.

prompt: The `pyang` output format that prints only the structure of a module is selected with `-f ___`.
hint: It is the shape the output has.

prompt: Why is `interfaces-state` still in the model if it is deprecated?
hint: Who would break if it vanished?

choices.text: Because the newer layout does not report counters, so this tree is where they live
choices.why: `statistics` is in the main tree too.

choices.text: So that clients written for the older model keep working
Because pyang cannot remove nodes
It holds the configuration of disabled interfaces, which the main tree leaves out

prompt: Match each kind of node to what it holds.

pairs.right: Several values of one type, with no key

prompt: Which line of `ietf-ip.yang` made `nc1` refuse a prefix length of 33?

choices.text: `if-feature ipv4-non-contiguous-netmasks`
The `range` on that leaf's `uint8` type
`type yang:dotted-quad`
A rule built into Clixon itself, for every interface it holds
choices.why: Clixon read it from the model.

prompt: In `ietf-ip`, `subnet` is a choice between `prefix-length` and `netmask`. What may an address carry?

choices.text: One of the two, never both at once
Both, as long as they agree
Neither
choices.why: One of them describes the subnet.

choices.text: A netmask
choices.why: Only if the device supports the feature, and the other alternative exists too.

prompt: A named, restricted type defined once and reused, like `inet:ipv4-address`, is declared with the YANG statement ___.
How does `ietf-ip` put addresses under an interface defined in `ietf-interfaces`?
hint: It adds nodes into another module's node.

choices.text: By copying the whole interface list into its own module
By asking the device to merge the two files at boot
choices.why: The models relate by augment, not by merging files.

choices.text: By a deviation that replaces `ietf-interfaces`
choices.why: A deviation declares a difference from a model.

choices.text: By `augment`

prompt: In RESTCONF JSON, why is the key `"ietf-ip:ipv4"` though it sits inside an `ietf-interfaces` interface?

choices.text: Because JSON keys are unique across the whole document, and `ipv4` appears elsewhere in the tree
choices.why: The prefix names the module, not a uniqueness rule.

choices.text: Because the module that defined it is `ietf-ip`
choices.why: Right: a node carries its defining module.

choices.text: Because RESTCONF prefixes every key
It is a Clixon convention with no standard behind it, specific to nc1

prompt: Which are true of OpenConfig's `openconfig-interfaces`, as the tree showed it? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Each interface has a `config` container and a `state` container
It keeps state in a separate `interfaces-state` tree
choices.why: That was the old IETF arrangement.

choices.text: It is published by the IETF
`state` repeats leaves of `config` and adds ones only the device knows

prompt: A team automates 300 devices from four vendors. When does a native model make sense?

choices.text: For what the standard models do not cover, accepting the tie to one vendor
Wherever possible, as native models parse faster
In no case, since standard models are enough
When the devices come from a single vendor
choices.why: Mixed networks use native models too, where the standard stops.

prompt: A script asks the `running` datastore for `oper-status`. What does it get?

choices.text: Nothing: it is state
The current oper-status
choices.why: State lives in the operational datastore.

choices.text: An error: oper-status does not exist
The last configured value

prompt: Match each protocol to what it allows on a state (`ro`) node.
Since NMDA, everything a device is actually using, configured or learnt, is in the ___ datastore.
Which first check should a troubleshooting script report, according to the section?

choices.text: Counters above zero on the device's interfaces
choices.why: Traffic is normal, not a problem.

choices.text: Interfaces enabled in configuration and down in state
Interfaces whose description is empty or too short to read
Nodes marked `x--`, which the device should stop reporting

prompt: What does the `must` statement in `example-branches` enforce?

choices.text: That an active branch has at least one DNS server
That every branch has a name of at most 32 characters
That the LAN is a /26
That ids are unique

prompt: `yanglint -p ietf example-branches.yang branches.json` printed nothing. What does that mean?

choices.text: The data is valid against the model, exit status 0
It could not find the data file and gave up quietly
The model is empty
It needs `-v`
choices.why: Silence is its answer for valid data.

prompt: Match each broken file to the line of the module that caught it.
With which exit status did `yanglint` end for each invalid data file?
A branch in `branches.json` lists three DNS servers. Which statement of the module refuses it?

choices.text: `must "status != 'active' or dns-server"`
choices.why: That asks for at least one, not at most two.

choices.text: `type inet:ipv4-address`, whose pattern refuses a third entry
choices.why: The type checks each address, not their number.

choices.text: `max-elements 2`
None: it would be accepted

prompt: Why did `nc1` refuse the branches with `unknown-namespace`?

choices.text: It does not have the `example-branches` model
Because the JSON in `branches.json` was malformed and could not be read
Because RESTCONF accepts XML in a POST, not JSON
choices.why: It accepts JSON, as lesson 3 showed.

choices.text: Because branch 3 has no DNS server, which the must refuses
choices.why: Branch 3 is planned, and the data was valid.

prompt: What does the revision next to each module in the yang-library tell you?
